senses.definition: very skilled or proficient at something
senses.example: After years of practice she was adept at reading the rhythm of a negotiation.

senses.definition: concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty
senses.example: The architect made the choice for aesthetic reasons rather than practical ones.

senses.definition: a set of principles underlying the look of an artist's work or a style
senses.example: The film's aesthetic borrows heavily from old travel posters.

senses.definition: selfless concern for the well-being of others
senses.example: The donor's altruism was clear: she gave anonymously and asked for nothing.

senses.definition: open and responsive to suggestion; easily persuaded
senses.example: The landlord was amenable to a shorter lease.

senses.definition: (of a thing) able to be treated or dealt with in a particular way
senses.example: The disease is amenable to treatment if caught early.

senses.definition: to cause someone to become hostile
senses.example: His habit of interrupting antagonized everyone at the table.

senses.definition: based on chance or personal whim rather than on reason or a system
senses.example: The order of the speakers was arbitrary; they drew names from a hat.

senses.definition: able to express ideas clearly and effectively
senses.example: The most articulate student was chosen to present the project.

senses.definition: to express an idea or feeling clearly in words
senses.example: She struggled to articulate why the plan worried her.

senses.definition: gentle and kindly
senses.example: Her benign smile put the nervous children at ease.

senses.definition: (of a disease or growth) not harmful
senses.example: The tests showed that the lump was benign.

senses.definition: high-sounding but with little meaning; inflated
senses.example: The candidate's bombastic promises impressed few voters.

senses.definition: inclined to agree with others or obey rules
senses.example: The new manager wanted a compliant staff, not a thoughtful one.

senses.definition: meeting rules or standards
senses.example: All new buildings must be compliant with the fire code.

senses.definition: causing or likely to cause an argument; controversial
senses.example: The new stadium was a contentious issue in the election.

senses.definition: (of a person) given to arguing
senses.example: A contentious man, he disputed every item on the bill.

senses.definition: too ready to believe things; gullible
senses.example: Credulous buyers paid a fortune for the fake painting.

words.note: Credulous means too ready to believe; credible means believable.

senses.definition: having a meaning that is mysterious or obscure
senses.example: He left a cryptic message: "Check the old oak."

senses.definition: a scarcity or lack of something
senses.example: There is a dearth of reliable data on the subject.

senses.definition: behavior in keeping with good taste and propriety
senses.example: Even in defeat, the team behaved with decorum.

senses.definition: humble submission and respect
senses.example: Out of deference to her age, they let her speak first.

senses.definition: imitative of the work of another person; unoriginal
senses.example: The band's second album was derivative and dull.

senses.definition: something based on another source
senses.example: French is a derivative of Latin.

senses.definition: a forceful and bitter verbal attack
senses.example: The meeting ended with a long diatribe against the city council.

senses.definition: drawing ideas, style or taste from a broad and diverse range of sources
senses.example: The café's eclectic menu includes ramen, tacos and borscht.

senses.definition: mental calmness and composure, especially in a difficult situation
senses.example: She accepted the bad news with remarkable equanimity.

senses.definition: open to more than one interpretation; deliberately ambiguous
senses.example: The senator gave an equivocal answer that pleased no one.

senses.definition: uncertain or questionable
senses.example: The results of the trial were equivocal.

senses.definition: very attentive to accuracy and detail
senses.example: The fastidious editor caught every misplaced comma.

senses.definition: very concerned about cleanliness; hard to please
senses.example: He was so fastidious that he wiped down every restaurant table.

senses.definition: to encourage or promote the development of something
senses.example: The program aims to foster a love of reading.

senses.definition: to bring up a child that is not one's own
senses.example: They have fostered more than twenty children over the years.

senses.definition: sparing or economical with money or food
senses.example: By living frugally, they saved enough for a house.

senses.definition: a belief or opinion contrary to accepted religious doctrine
senses.example: In the sixteenth century, the scholar was tried for heresy.

senses.definition: an opinion profoundly at odds with what is generally accepted
senses.example: In this office, suggesting a four-day week is heresy.

senses.definition: having no particular interest or sympathy; unconcerned
senses.example: He was indifferent to the outcome of the game.

senses.definition: neither good nor bad; mediocre
senses.example: The restaurant served indifferent food at high prices.

senses.definition: existing in something as a permanent, essential or characteristic attribute
senses.example: There are risks inherent in any surgery.

senses.definition: inborn; natural
senses.example: She had an innate sense of rhythm.

senses.definition: fearless; adventurous
senses.example: The intrepid explorers crossed the ice cap on foot.

senses.definition: able to be hammered or pressed into shape without breaking
senses.example: Gold is the most malleable of all metals.

senses.definition: easily influenced; pliable
senses.example: The cult targeted young and malleable recruits.

senses.definition: showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise
senses.example: The restoration was carried out with meticulous care.

senses.definition: a person who is new to a subject, skill or belief
senses.example: The class is designed for neophytes with no coding experience.

senses.definition: stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or chosen course of action
senses.example: The obstinate mule refused to cross the bridge.

senses.definition: giving the impression that something bad is going to happen
senses.example: Ominous clouds gathered over the hills.

senses.definition: a person or thing regarded as a perfect example of a particular quality
senses.example: The knight was a paragon of courage and courtesy.

senses.definition: not securely held or in position; dangerously likely to fall or collapse
senses.example: The vase sat in a precarious position at the edge of the shelf.

senses.definition: dependent on chance; uncertain
senses.example: Freelancers often live a precarious existence.

senses.definition: (of an artist or author) producing many works
senses.example: The prolific novelist published two books a year.

senses.definition: (of a plant, animal or person) producing much fruit or many offspring
senses.example: Rabbits are prolific breeders.

senses.definition: acting with or showing care and thought for the future
senses.example: It would be prudent to save some of the bonus.

senses.definition: deep regret or guilt for a wrong committed
senses.example: He showed no remorse for the crime.

senses.definition: feeling or showing deep and solemn respect
senses.example: A reverent hush fell over the crowd at the memorial.

senses.definition: to examine or inspect closely and thoroughly
senses.example: The editor scrutinized every claim in the article.

senses.definition: tending to induce drowsiness or sleep
senses.example: The professor's soporific voice put half the class to sleep.

senses.definition: to waste something, especially money or time, in a reckless and foolish manner
senses.example: He squandered his savings on lottery tickets.

senses.definition: to provide evidence to support or prove the truth of
senses.example: The journalist could not substantiate the rumor.

senses.definition: kept secret, especially because it would not be approved of
senses.example: He cast a surreptitious glance at his phone during the meeting.

senses.definition: sparing in the use of words; abrupt
senses.example: Her terse reply made it clear she was annoyed.

senses.definition: showing or suffering from nervousness or a lack of confidence
senses.example: A timorous knock came at the door.

senses.definition: eager or quick to argue or fight; aggressively defiant
senses.example: The truculent customer threatened to sue.

senses.definition: to waver between different opinions or actions; to be indecisive
senses.example: She vacillated between the two job offers for weeks.

senses.definition: conformity to facts; accuracy
senses.example: Reporters checked the veracity of the claims.

senses.definition: habitual truthfulness
senses.example: No one doubted the witness's veracity.
